advances: Closes the entire \(p_\varnothing=0\) opposite-pair branch, classifies the surviving positive-\(p_\varnothing\) opposite support into two minimal path types up to relabeling, and derives the exact endpoint-plus-slab budget forced by \(W=0\).  An exact connected-support scalar calibration satisfies the crossings, both tails, finite interior, \(W=0\), and every endpoint/slab capacity used in that budget.  Hence the first still-missing input is a genuinely simultaneous common-plane convex-realizability inequality, equivalently a constrained section or mixed-area charge for the three target caps; no rearrangement of these listed scalar constraints can close the branch.
author: mp_r60_opposite_support_closure
proof:
Accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f` gives
\[
P_N=Q_\varnothing=R_\varnothing=\varnothing.
\tag{15}
\]
Consequently the only negative coefficient in (4) belongs to
\(P_\varnothing\): every nonempty-index cell has coefficient at least
\(1\).  If \(p_\varnothing=0\), then (5) gives directly
\[
W\ge q_{\{j\}}+4q_{\{k,\ell\}}>0,
\]
contrary to \(W=0\).  This proves (6).

We next prove the support classification.  In the affine coordinates
\[
q_i=f_i+L_i,
\]
the three cutting lines \(q_i=0\) are pairwise nonparallel and
\[
q_1+q_2+q_3=-\sigma
\]
for some \(\sigma>0\).  Their seven chambers have adjacency graph consisting of the outer cycle
\[
\{3\},\{1,3\},\{1\},\{1,2\},\{2\},\{2,3\}
\tag{16}
\]
and the central chamber \(N\), adjacent exactly to the three doubleton chambers.

The positive-area support of a convex two-dimensional \(A_2\) is connected in this graph.  Indeed, positive area in a cell supplies a strict point of
\(\operatorname{int}A_2\) in that chamber.  The segment between two such points lies in
\(\operatorname{int}A_2\).  If it crosses one cutting line at a time, the successive chambers form an adjacency path.  If it meets two cutting lines simultaneously, a small ball about that interior point lies in \(A_2\) and meets all four local chambers, again supplying an adjacency path.  Three lines cannot meet because their coordinate sum is \(-\sigma\ne0\).

In the graph (16), the graph distance from \(\{j\}\) to
\(\{k,\ell\}\) is three.  Its four shortest paths are exactly
(7a)--(7d).  If \(N\) is absent from a connected support containing the two endpoints, the support lies in the outer six-cycle and must contain one of the two three-edge arcs between the antipodal vertices.  If \(N\) is present, then the supported edge \(N-\{k,\ell\}\), together with any path from \(\{j\}\) to \(N\), forces either
\[
\{j\}-\{j,k\}-N-\{k,\ell\}
\]
or
\[
\{j\}-\{j,\ell\}-N-\{k,\ell\}.
\]
Thus every connected support containing the opposite pair contains one of (7a)--(7d).  This refines the forced chamber-filling conclusion of accepted fact `78d1d57e3961c4e4`.

For completeness, both minimal types are genuinely realizable at the \(Q\)-body level.  Normalize to
\[
q_1+q_2+q_3=-1
\]
and take \((j,k,\ell)=(3,1,2)\).  The segment joining
\[
x=\left(\frac1{10},\frac9{10},-2\right)
\quad\hbox{to}\quad
y=\left(-\frac{29}{10},-\frac1{10},2\right)
\]
crosses \(q_1=0,q_3=0,q_2=0\) at the distinct parameter values
\[
\frac1{30},\qquad\frac12,\qquad\frac9{10},
\]
so its successive strict chambers are
\[
\{3\},\{1,3\},\{1\},\{1,2\}.
\]
The segment joining the same \(x\) to
\[
y'=\left(-1,-\frac1{10},\frac1{10}\right)
\]
crosses \(q_1=0,q_2=0,q_3=0\) at
\[
\frac1{11},\qquad\frac9{10},\qquad\frac{20}{21},
\]
so its successive strict chambers are
\[
\{3\},\{1,3\},N,\{1,2\}.
\]
For either segment, its Minkowski sum with a sufficiently small centrally symmetric two-dimensional polygon meets exactly the four displayed chambers, each in positive area.  Permuting \(k,\ell\) gives the other two paths.  This proves all claims in part 2.

Now assume \(p_\varnothing>0\) and define
\[
U=\frac{P_\varnothing+E}{2},\qquad
V=\frac{P_\varnothing+F}{2},\qquad
D=Z\cap\{-1<f_j<0\}.
\]
Accepted facts `c472ceb412ca0594` and `9922bcace1cdc113`, together with the exact incidence table in `0e51a47a9add571f`, give
\[
U\subseteq R_{\{j\}},
\tag{17}
\]
\[
V\subseteq R_{\{k\}}\sqcup R_{\{\ell\}}\sqcup R_{\{k,\ell\}},
\tag{18}
\]
\[
D\subseteq R_{\{j,k\}}\sqcup R_{\{j,\ell\}}\sqcup R_N,
\qquad |D|=s_j>0.
\tag{19}
\]
They are pairwise disjoint because they lie respectively in
\[
f_j<-1,\qquad f_j>0,\qquad -1<f_j<0.
\]
The weighted \(R\)-contribution is therefore at least
\[
|U|+|V|+4s_j.
\tag{20}
\]
The two endpoint Brunn--Minkowski bounds in accepted fact
`9922bcace1cdc113` give
\[
|U|\ge
\frac14\left(\sqrt{p_\varnothing}+
\sqrt{q_{\{j\}}}\right)^2,
\tag{21}
\]
\[
|V|\ge
\frac14\left(\sqrt{p_\varnothing}+
\sqrt{q_{\{k,\ell\}}}\right)^2.
\tag{22}
\]
The displayed opposite \(Q\)-cells contribute
\[
q_{\{j\}}+4q_{\{k,\ell\}}
\tag{23}
\]
to \(W\).  All uncounted nonempty-index cell contributions are nonnegative.  Since (15) and \(W=0\) say that the total positive contribution is exactly
\(2p_\varnothing\), adding (20)--(23) proves (8).

It remains to verify the scalar calibration.  From (9)--(12),
\[
M=1,\qquad m=\frac1{10},\qquad k=1,
\tag{24}
\]
and
\[
(u_1,u_2,u_3)
=
\left(\frac{49}{1000},\frac1{20},\frac1{20}\right),
\tag{25}
\]
\[
(v_1,v_2,v_3)
=
\left(\frac{51}{1000},\frac1{20},\frac{99}{2000}\right),
\tag{26}
\]
\[
(c_1,c_2,c_3)
=
\left(\frac{11}{30},\frac{11}{30},
\frac{11}{30}+\frac1{2000}\right).
\tag{27}
\]
Thus all nine quantities in (25)--(27) are strictly between zero and their ambient totals.  Moreover,
\[
u_i+v_i+c_i=\frac7{15}
=\frac29\left(1+\frac1{10}+1\right)
\qquad(i=1,2,3),
\tag{28}
\]
so all crossings hold.  The left tails are equalities for \(i=1,2\) and strict for \(i=3\):
\[
c_1+m=c_2+m=\frac7{15},\qquad
c_3+m=\frac7{15}+\frac1{2000}.
\tag{29}
\]
All right tails are strict because \(c_i+M>7/15\).

The three weighted contributions are
\[
W_P=-\frac{1553}{1000}=-\frac{3106}{2000},
\tag{30}
\]
\[
W_Q=q_1+q_3+4q_{12}+4q_{13}
=\frac{503}{2000},
\tag{31}
\]
\[
W_R=r_1+r_2+r_3+4r_{12}+4r_{13}
=\frac{2603}{2000}.
\tag{32}
\]
Hence \(W=0\) exactly.  The support (13) is the outer path in (7a), so the calibration respects not merely the weak bridge conclusion of
`78d1d57e3961c4e4` but the full connected-support requirement.

Finally set
\[
A=
\frac14\left(\sqrt{\frac{851}{1000}}+
\sqrt{\frac{49}{1000}}\right)^2,
\qquad
B=
\frac14\left(\sqrt{\frac{851}{1000}}+
\sqrt{\frac1{20}}\right)^2.
\]
Since \(\sqrt{851}<30\) and \(\sqrt{1702}<42\),
\[
A<\frac{33}{100},\qquad
B<\frac{1321}{4000}.
\tag{33}
\]
The available exact target capacities are
\[
r_3=\frac{1097}{3000}>A,
\tag{34}
\]
\[
r_1+r_2+r_{12}
=\frac{3797}{6000}>B,
\tag{35}
\]
\[
r_{13}=\frac3{2000}>s_3=\frac1{1000},
\tag{36}
\]
and
\[
k=1>A+B+s_3.
\tag{37}
\]
The necessary budget (8) also has ample slack:
\[
q_3+4q_{12}+A+B+4s_3
<
\frac{3653}{4000}
<
2p_\varnothing.
\tag{38}
\]
Thus the crossings, tails, finite-interior constraints, \(W=0\), the exact connected opposite support, and every separate endpoint/slab scalar capacity are mutually consistent.  What the calibration omits is exactly the simultaneous transverse placement of all these subsets inside one compatible convex triple.  This proves the asserted reduction and identifies the first missing geometric quantity.
statement:
Let \(N=\{1,2,3\}\), and assume the common-plane hypotheses and exact-cell convention of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`.  Thus
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,\qquad L_1+L_2+L_3<-1,
\]
\(A_0,A_2,K\) are nonempty two-dimensional convex polytopes,
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K,
\]
and \(P_J,Q_H,R_G\) are the exact sign cells from that fact.  Write
\[
p_J=|P_J|,\qquad q_H=|Q_H|,\qquad r_G=|R_G|,
\]
\[
M=|A_0|,\qquad m=|A_2|,\qquad k=|K|,
\]
\[
u_i=\sum_{J\ni i}p_J,\qquad
v_i=\sum_{H\ni i}q_H,\qquad
c_i=\sum_{G\ni i}r_G,
\]
and
\[
t=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9.
\]
Assume the three crossings
\[
u_i+v_i+c_i=t\qquad(i\in N),
\tag{1}
\]
the canonical tails
\[
c_i+m\ge t,\qquad c_i+M>t\qquad(i\in N),
\tag{2}
\]
and finite interior
\[
0<u_i<M,\qquad 0<v_i<m,\qquad 0<c_i<k
\qquad(i\in N).
\tag{3}
\]
Put
\[
W=
\sum_J(3|J|-2)p_J+
\sum_H(3|H|-2)q_H+
\sum_G(3|G|-2)r_G,
\tag{4}
\]
and assume \(W=0\).  Fix \(j\in N\), write
\[
N\setminus\{j\}=\{k,\ell\},
\]
and assume the opposite pair
\[
q_{\{j\}}>0,\qquad q_{\{k,\ell\}}>0.
\tag{5}
\]

Then:

1. Necessarily
\[
p_\varnothing>0.
\tag{6}
\]

2. The positive \(Q\)-support contains at least one of the four paths
\[
\{\{j\},\{j,k\},\{k\},\{k,\ell\}\},
\tag{7a}
\]
\[
\{\{j\},\{j,\ell\},\{\ell\},\{k,\ell\}\},
\tag{7b}
\]
\[
\{\{j\},\{j,k\},N,\{k,\ell\}\},
\tag{7c}
\]
\[
\{\{j\},\{j,\ell\},N,\{k,\ell\}\}.
\tag{7d}
\]
Up to interchanging \(k,\ell\), these are exactly two minimal types: an outer path and a path through \(N\).  Each of the four sets in (7) is realizable as the exact positive-area support of a two-dimensional convex polytope for the same affine sign arrangement.  This assertion concerns the \(Q\)-body alone and does not assert a full realization of (1)--(5).

3. Put
\[
E=\overline{Q_{\{j\}}},\qquad
F=\overline{Q_{\{k,\ell\}}},\qquad
H=\operatorname{conv}(E\cup F),
\]
\[
Z=\frac{P_\varnothing+H}{2},\qquad
s_j=|Z\cap\{-1<f_j<0\}|.
\]
Accepted facts `c472ceb412ca0594` and `9922bcace1cdc113` give \(s_j>0\).  Every realization satisfying (1)--(5) obeys the necessary budget
\[
\begin{aligned}
2p_\varnothing\ge{}&
q_{\{j\}}+4q_{\{k,\ell\}}\\
&+\frac14\left(\sqrt{p_\varnothing}+
\sqrt{q_{\{j\}}}\right)^2
+\frac14\left(\sqrt{p_\varnothing}+
\sqrt{q_{\{k,\ell\}}}\right)^2
+4s_j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Thus the strict slab is already charged inside the positive \(R\)-cell budget; (8) is a necessary inequality, not a contradiction.

4. The following exact nonnegative scalar table shows that the numerical conditions in (1)--(5), the connected outer-path support in (7a), and all endpoint/slab capacities used in (8) are jointly consistent.  Take
\[
(j,k,\ell)=(3,1,2)
\]
and set every unlisted cell mass to zero.  Put
\[
p_\varnothing=\frac{851}{1000},\qquad
p_1=\frac{49}{1000},\qquad
p_2=p_3=\frac1{20},
\tag{9}
\]
\[
q_3=\frac{49}{1000},\qquad
q_{12}=\frac1{20},\qquad
q_{13}=q_1=\frac1{2000},
\tag{10}
\]
\[
r_1=\frac4{15}-\frac1{2000},\qquad
r_2=\frac4{15}+\frac1{1000},\qquad
r_3=\frac{11}{30}-\frac1{1000},
\tag{11}
\]
\[
r_{12}=\frac1{10}-\frac1{1000},\qquad
r_{13}=\frac3{2000}.
\tag{12}
\]
It has exact \(Q\)-support
\[
\{3,13,1,12\},
\tag{13}
\]
and one may assign
\[
s_3=\frac1{1000}<r_{13}.
\tag{14}
\]
This is a scalar calibration, not a claimed common-plane convex realization.  Therefore the first missing datum is precisely a theorem coupling the transverse placement of the endpoint images and the slab inside all three target caps.  Equivalently, one needs a constrained fiber-transport or mixed-area inequality for \(Z\) that is not determined by the cell masses, the crossings, the tails, or the separate Brunn--Minkowski bounds.
